newsitem.title: UK: Unilever chief says UK must sign up for EMU.
newsitem.headline: Unilever chief says UK must sign up for EMU.

text.p: Britain is becoming marginalised in Europe and cannot afford to stand outside a single currency in the long term, the chairman of cosmetics-to-detergents giant Unilever Plc said on Tuesday.

Niall Fitzgerald, who is also chairman of the Confederation of British Industry's Europe committee, told the CBI's annual conference that time was running out for Britain to change its approach with the European Union set to make key decisions on European Economic and Monetary Union in the next year.
"We have to recognise that our Maastricht manoeuvring has tried the patience of our partners to the point which they now frequently ignore our incomprehensible mutterings," he said.
He said in the longer-term, opting out of a single currency was not an option.
"And to go further and actually rule out joining the single currency now would be the height of folly and I am glad that both party leaders have resisted the siren voices."

"Staying out and seeing if it works is not a policy, not even an opt-out but a cop out," Fitzgerald said. "It is my strong personal conviction that we must be prepared to take a clear position on EMU and a single currency by mid-1997."
He said Britain had a history of standing apart from closer European integration only to acquiesce later.
If this were to happen on a single currency the consequences could be disastrous and the consequences of Britain being outside the core are very serious.
